newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto says Indonesia vulnerable to drug trade.
newsitem.headline: Suharto says Indonesia vulnerable to drug trade.

text.p: President Suharto said on Monday Indonesia was particularly exposed to drug trafficking because of its geographical location.

"We are aware that our country, which has a population of around 200 million and consists of thousands of small and big islands in the crossroads between oceans, is a vulnerable place for drug trafficking," Suharto said while inaugurating a conference of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) for the prevention of drug abuse.
"Nations all over the world must forge an even closer cooperation in the fight against drug and substance abuse," Suharto said.

"We are increasingly concerned about the number of our young people who become drug addicts today...this will certainly lead to social unrest and jeopardise the development of potential human resources."
The drug Ecstasy has gained wide popularity in Indonesian cities in recent years.
Numerous high-profile arrests have led to calls for stricter controls on the drug. A bill that will give authorities more power in their fight against Ecstasy is before parliament.
Earlier this year, a pilot with Indonesia's national airline Garuda was arrested by Dutch police as he boarded a plane at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport with 8,000 Ecstasy pills strapped to his waist.
The Netherlands refused to extradite the pilot, who faces charges in a Dutch court.
Last month, an Indonesian television actress arrested for possesion of almost 30,000 Ecstasy pills escaped from police custody after being allowed to go home for a bath.
Indonesian police tracked her down in the United States and brought her back to face drug trafficking charges.
